A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Gaze-LLE and contain complete main text and supplementary material. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison after matching section renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original gaze-estimation experiments on four datasets, architectural ablations, runtime measurements, and supplementary robustness and failure-case analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in the main paper and supplement.

M1.justification: The frozen DINOv2 encoder, head-position prompting, transformer decoder, prediction heads, and training objectives are unchanged. Integrating head detection into the shared features is newly suggested as future work, not implemented.

E1.justification: Both versions use GazeFollow, VideoAttentionTarget, ChildPlay, and GOO-Real with the same gaze-estimation, in/out prediction, and cross-dataset evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main and supplementary experiments. The new ViTGaze section discusses that method but adds no evaluated comparison or scores.

E3.justification: The reported training schedules, tested configurations, input/output resolutions, metrics, and matching procedures are retained. ViTGaze's higher input resolution and postprocessing are discussed without being adopted in the experiments.

E4.justification: The backbone and head-prompt ablations, input-resolution tests, detection-matching analysis, runtime scaling, estimated-head-box evaluation, LoRA experiments, and failure cases are retained. Renumbered supplementary sections contain the same analyses.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version provides repeated-seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the reported benchmark results.

E6.justification: Table 3 revises Sharingan's reported learnable parameter count from an estimated greater than 135M to 105M. The matched accuracy scores, ablation results, runtime findings, and qualitative examples remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, model and loss equations, detection-matching costs, and field-of-view construction are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same core contributions: gaze estimation using frozen foundation features and a lightweight prompted decoder, strong benchmark and cross-dataset performance, and efficient training.

C2.justification: New supplementary Section 10 discusses feature reuse, ViTGaze's potential advantages for on-device deployment, and differences in prediction postprocessing. Section 11 adds a future direction involving head detection from shared frozen features.

D1.justification: Table 3 revises technical documentation of Sharingan's parameter count without identifying a different tested architecture. Other implementation recipes and access information are retained; v1 already announces code and model release in its introduction.

R1.justification: v2 adds a dedicated discussion of concurrent ViTGaze and references to ViTGaze, GazeTransformer, and coordinate postprocessing. Section 2 also softens its broad characterization of multi-branch architectures as unnecessary and inefficient while retaining the frozen-encoder novelty claim.

P1.justification: Changes include localized related-work rewriting, a short new supplementary section, more specific cross-references, subsequent section renumbering, and author-affiliation and contribution-footnote updates. The overall narrative and organization remain stable.

P2.justification: The existing figures and tables are retained. Table 1 has clearer baseline labels, page numbers are added, and supplementary content is rearranged, including moving Table 17 to PDF page 19 and the failure-case discussion beside Figure 10 on page 21.

improvement.justification: The ViTGaze discussion fills a limited gap in research positioning and gives a more balanced account of deployment tradeoffs and evaluation differences. Clearer supplementary references and table labels also improve readability. These are modest gains; the method and empirical support remain essentially unchanged.
